update_message: Pseudonyx policy update: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (m365.cloud.microsoft) and the Claude Console (platform.claude.com) are now redacted like the other AI sites, instead of being closed or unwatched.
previous_update_message: Pseudonyx policy update: video, audio, RAW photo, medical scan, design, disk image and key files are no longer sent to AI sites unchanged; they are refused, because they can carry personal data Pseudonyx cannot pseudonymise.

_note: download_url MUST start with licensing.downloadUrlAllowedPrefix in settings.json, currently
https://downloads.pseudonyx.org/releases/. The client REFUSES anything outside that prefix, so a URL
pointing anywhere else does not merely fail to download - it is dropped before any request is made and
no update can reach an installed user. Keys are immutable and versioned: never overwrite one.
latest_version TRACKS THE SOURCE BUILD and is asserted equal to the csproj <Version> by
VersionSingleSourceTests. An earlier note here said not to raise it until the R2 object exists, which
is a rule this repository breaks on every commit and a test enforces breaking - the two could not both
be obeyed, and the test won silently. HUMAN-ACTIONS 4b already documents the real consequence: on a
build that was copied rather than released, an update check offers a version it cannot fetch, and that
is expected rather than a bug.
WHAT ACTUALLY PROTECTS A USER IS THE ABSENCE OF THE OTHER TWO KEYS. installer_url and sha256 are what
UpdateDownloader needs, and a missing hash is refused exactly like a wrong one - so with them absent
nothing can auto-install and the app offers the download instead. Publish BOTH, together, only once the
signed object is in R2, and only with the POST-signing hash. Adding either one early is the only edit
here that can make a client execute a file.
download_url carries the version TWICE and must agree with latest_version; that is asserted by a test
now, because this URL has been hand-edited and left stale before - it sat at 1.10.22 while
latest_version said 1.10.24, so an install was told one version and handed another.

_what_this_is: Which browsers Pseudonyx SUPPORTS, meaning the browser where the live-typing extension, the native
bridge and the send-time verification have actually been exercised end to end. Chrome and Edge are
the two that have; every other browser is listed as unsupported and is therefore BLOCKED by default.
Blocking a browser is not the same thing as not protecting it. An unsupported browser is one where a
message could leave while the app still reported protection, and that is the single failure this
product exists to prevent. So the default answer is to close the browser rather than to watch it
with machinery nobody has verified there.
The user owns the final answer. Settings > Blocked browsers lists every browser here and the choice
is stored per browser in browsers.json, so a decision made by hand outlives any change to this file.
Supported: false + the user unticking it is a supported combination and it is honoured.
Names MUST match Live.BrowserCatalog exactly. A name that does not appear in the catalog can never
be identified on the wire, so it could never be enforced either; BrowserSupportListTests fails the
build rather than shipping an entry that silently does nothing.
File types Pseudonyx CANNOT redact, and that carry no personal data, so they must NOT be blocked. A
font, an installer or model weights has no text a person wrote, so refusing the upload buys nothing:
it only stops people working. Anything listed here is passed to the site exactly as they chose it.
IT LIVES IN companies.json ON PURPOSE. This is the file the application already re-syncs every day, so
a format we discover we cannot redact can be let through by a list update rather than by a release. It
used to be a standalone passthrough-extensions.json with a byte-identical copy inside the extension,
kept in step by a script and a drift test - two files, a tool and a test to say one thing.
THE BROWSER EXTENSION DOES NOT READ THIS FILE. It asks the application, which serves the list already
FILTERED through its own classifier. That matters because this file is remote-updatable: a bad list
push that added .pdf here could otherwise have sent documents to a model untouched. The application
drops any entry it recognises as redactable and logs it, so neither reader can be talked into a leak.
Re-read whenever this file changes, not once at startup. The extension re-pulls within one keep-alive
ping, because the ping already reports a stamp of these policy files and it already re-pulls on change.
_the_one_rule: ONLY put an extension here if we genuinely cannot redact it. This list is a hole in the protection by
design, so every entry must earn its place by being impossible rather than merely inconvenient.
In particular, DO NOT ADD:
- Images (.png .jpg .webp .gif .bmp .tiff .heic ...). Pseudonyx redacts these: it reads text out of
them with OCR and paints over it, and it detects and covers faces. They are among the most
valuable things it protects, not an exception to it.
- Documents (.pdf .docx .xlsx .pptx .odt .rtf .epub ...). All extracted and redacted.
- Anything text-shaped at all (.txt .csv .json .srt .vcf .sql, source code, config, notebooks).
See FileClassifier: unknown extensions that merely LOOK like text are redacted in place too, so
adding a text format here would create a leak in a format we handle perfectly well.
If you are unsure whether something is redactable, leave it out. Leaving it out means it is checked
and possibly refused, which is the safe direction; putting it in means it goes to the AI untouched.
AND NO AMBIGUOUS EXTENSIONS. Several extensions mean two unrelated things, and where one meaning is a
text format the entry has to go. Four were removed after being caught by a test rather than by eye:
.ts   MPEG transport stream, but overwhelmingly more often TypeScript source
.asm  a CATIA assembly, but also assembly-language source
.vhd  a Hyper-V disk image, but also VHDL source
.cue  a CD cue sheet, but also the CUE configuration language - and cue sheets are plain text anyway
The application would have survived all four, because FileClassifier checks its text tiers BEFORE this
list. So would the extension NOW, because the application filters the list before serving it. Neither
of those is a reason to leave a wrong entry here: a filtered-out entry is a line that reads as
protection-off and does nothing, and the next person to look will not know which of the two it is. A
test asserts the intersection with the redactable tiers is empty.
One extension, one dot. An entry like ".sav.spss" matches nothing at all - both readers key on the
final extension - so it is not a harmless extra, it is a line that looks like protection and is not.
_the_bytes_decide: SINCE 31 OCTOBER 2026 THIS LIST IS NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT. An extension here used to be the whole
decision: the file went to the AI service on its NAME, so a customers.csv renamed customers.bin, a text
export a tool had called .dat, or anything at all called .mp4 went through with every record intact
(audit finding D1/B5). The application now reads the bytes of every file first (FileContentSniffer) and a
listed extension passes ONLY when the bytes carry the signature that extension is supposed to have: an
ftyp box in a .mp4, an MZ header in an .exe, a ZIP in a .jar. Text under any of these names is redacted
as text and keeps its name. Unknown bytes under any of these names are refused and the user is told.
Two consequences for whoever edits this file. First, an entry whose format has no signature the sniffer
can verify is INERT - its files are examined like any other - so prefer removing such an entry to leaving
a line that reads as protection-off. Second, the record-bearing formats that used to sit here (.bin, .img,
.core, .sas7bdat, .xpt) are gone and are named in FileClassifier.DataContainers, so a synced copy of
this file cannot bring them back: the loader drops them as it reads.

why: THE `archives` GROUP WAS DELETED, and this note is here so nobody adds it back.
It listed .zip .rar .7z .tar .gz and about thirty more as pass-through, and its own note admitted
the cost: 'a zip of CVs now reaches the AI unredacted'. That was the largest deliberate gap in the
product.
What happens now. FileClassifier gives archives their own tier: the archive is unpacked, every file
inside is pseudonymised through the same ladder as a loose document, entry names are pseudonymised
too, and it is repacked - provided the whole round trip fits in three seconds. If it does not, or
the format cannot be opened (.7z, .rar), the archive is REFUSED rather than sent.
Do not re-add these extensions. IsFormatWeRedact now claims them, so the loader would drop them as
it reads the file - and a line that reads as protection-off while doing nothing is worse than no
line, which is what No_pass_through_extension_is_also_a_format_we_can_redact asserts against the
raw file rather than the filtered list.
Note the packaged DOCUMENT formats that are technically zips - .docx .xlsx .pptx .odt .epub - were
never here. Those are recognised as documents and fully redacted.
SIX GROUPS WERE DELETED ON 1 NOVEMBER 2026 (app 2.0.3): video, audio, captured_and_scientific,
design_cad_and_3d, disk_and_system_images and encrypted_and_signed.
Each can carry personal data the product cannot pseudonymise: a voice or a face in a recording, a
person in a RAW photo, a patient in a NIfTI scan, names and faces in a Photoshop or CAD file, whole
folders of documents in a disk image, a person's name in a certificate. Passing them unchanged
contradicted the rule the product is sold on: pseudonymise, or block.
Now a file of these types is REFUSED on an AI site, with the usual 'not attached' notice naming the
file and the reason. Fonts, installers and model weights stay: they carry no personal data. An owner
who needs a deleted group back can re-add it here in a list update; the classifier still verifies
each file's bytes against its name.
Machine code. Nothing to redact, and rewriting a binary would corrupt it.
Note .obj is NOT here despite being a compiler's object file, because it is also the Wavefront 3D
format, which is plain text. Ambiguous wins go to the redactable meaning every time: a text .obj
now gets redacted, and a compiled one gets checked and possibly refused, which is the safe half.
.bin, .o, .a and .lib were REMOVED on 31 October 2026. .bin is what a renamed CSV, a firmware image and
a raw export all look like from the outside - a name that means nothing cannot earn a pass. Object files
and static libraries carry strings, symbols and build paths. All four are named in
FileClassifier.DataContainers so the loader drops them if a synced list re-adds them.

fonts.why: Glyph outlines and metrics tables. No user-authored content at all, and no text layer to rewrite.

why: THE `binary_data_and_databases` GROUP WAS DELETED ON 31 OCTOBER 2026, and this note is here so nobody
adds it back.
The 17 September fix took .db .sqlite .mdb .accdb .pst .ost .parquet .sav .dta .h5 out of it and left
the rest, and the rest was still records all the way down: database engines (.db3 .ldb .myd .myi .frm
.ibd .dbf .fdb .gdb), Notes and Exchange stores (.nsf .edb), embedded key-value stores (.realm
.leveldb .rocksdb), serialised records (.orc .feather .arrow .avro .pb .protobuf .msgpack .bson) and
data-science objects (.npy .npz .mat .rdata .rds .pickle .pkl .joblib). Pass-through means 'there was
never anything in this file we could have redacted', and every one of these is personal data in a
binary coat.
They are now all named in FileClassifier.DataContainers: Opaque by name, so a synced copy of this file
cannot bring them back (the loader drops them as it reads), and decided by their bytes like everything
else - a CSV somebody called .dbf is redacted as text, an SQLite file somebody called .mp4 is refused.

machine_learning_models.why: Weights. Enormous, opaque, and nothing a person wrote.

_what_this_is: Browser extensions Pseudonyx allows on EVERY PC. Every browser refuses every other extension, including ones an
IT department force-installs (ExtensionInstallForcelist), unless this list or the administrator's own list in
Settings > Browser Extensions names it. The two lists add up; the administrator's list travels in the signed team
policy as allowed_extensions. Pseudonyx's own extension is always allowed by the code, whatever this file says;
it is listed here so the list reads complete.
ONLY EXTENSIONS THAT DO NOT SEND PAGE CONTENT TO AN AI belong here: sign-in helpers and password managers that
companies rely on to work at all. Anything with an AI assistant, a writing aid or a page summariser stays out.
store is chrome (Chrome Web Store), edge (Edge Add-ons) or firefox (addons.mozilla.org); id is what the browser
policy keys on; name is shown in Settings. A wrong id is harmless (it allows nothing) and an invalid entry is
ignored. Verify a new id on its store page before adding it: the id is the last part of the store link.

_data_note: FIVE COMPANIES, FOURTEEN REDACTED HOSTS (2 November 2026). THE REDACTED TIER IS NOW, PER COMPANY, THE MOST-USED
SUBDOMAINS THAT CARRY AN AI CHAT BOX, AT MOST FIVE EACH, checked against public traffic data and vendor notices on
2 November 2026 (sources in docs/archi_and_specs/PROTECTION-COVERAGE.md, 'Redacted hosts'):
OpenAI      chatgpt.com (covers *.chatgpt.com), platform.openai.com (Playground). chat.openai.com only redirects
to chatgpt.com; sora.com / sora.chatgpt.com closed on 26 April 2026; openai.com has no chat box.
Google AI   gemini.google.com, notebook.google.com (Gemini Notebook since 16 July 2026), notebooklm.google.com
(old address, kept so a bookmark keeps cover), aistudio.google.com. labs.google stays BLOCKED (owner
decision of 18 October 2026) and google.com AI Mode is search, excluded for the bing.com reason.
Microsoft   copilot.microsoft.com, m365.cloud.microsoft (Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat; MOVED HERE FROM THE
BLOCKED TIER - Microsoft now redirects copilot.cloud.microsoft to m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, so the
enterprise chat had been closed outright), copilot.cloud.microsoft (kept for tenants and links not
yet redirected). bing.com stays out (owner decision of 7 September 2026).
Anthropic   claude.ai, platform.claude.com (the Console and its Workbench; the Console moved there from
console.anthropic.com, which is kept as the redirecting address). NOTE: both Console hosts are also
in the default Anthropic API block (AiApiBlocklist), so on a seat without the Claude relaxation they
do not open at all; listing them here is what protects them the day the owner relaxes it.
DeepSeek    chat.deepseek.com, deepseek.com (covers *.deepseek.com). platform.deepseek.com has no chat box.
Fewer than five where fewer exist: a host without a composer costs an access permission and buys nothing (the
30 August 2026 removals below). Every host here is exercised per channel by extension/tests/every-host-every-
channel.test.js and every-host-paste-upload-restore.test.js (typing, dictation, paste, text drop, upload button,
file drop, unredaction with no read-back), which read this file, so a host added here is tested automatically.
HISTORY. FOUR COMPANIES, SEVENTEEN WEBSITES, TWELVE REDACTED HOSTS (three were removed on 30 August 2026, below). This list was cut from 349 companies / 457 hosts to exactly
the four vendors and the websites named in docs/AI_Companies_Matrix.md. The matrix names twenty addresses,
but several are PATHS on one host (chatgpt.com/canvas, /sites, /voice; claude.ai/artifacts, /@projects), and
policy here is enforced per HOST - a path cannot be matched by the PAC, the proxy or a match pattern. So the
twenty collapse to the fifteen hosts below with no loss of coverage. Everything the product does is driven from
here: the PAC intercept set, the upload proxy, the blocking page, the extension's static match patterns
(generated - run tools/sync-extension-manifest.ps1) and the native-app gates. Adding a host here is a
protection decision, not a cosmetic one.
`verified` IS PER COMPANY, NOT PER HOST, and that used to matter for five of these addresses. THREE OF
THE FIVE ARE NOW GONE. `verified` means the site's own composer, send gesture and upload path have
actually been exercised, and it is what admits a host to the extension's static injection set. These
have been exercised: chatgpt.com, gemini.google.com, aistudio.google.com, notebooklm.google.com,
copilot.microsoft.com, claude.ai, console.anthropic.com. (huggingface.co and labs.google removed 18 Oct 2026).
REMOVED FROM THE REDACTED TIER on 7 September 2026, at the owner's request: bing.com. It was Microsoft AI's
third host and the only general-purpose search engine in the redacting set, which made it the one host where
the product decrypted and rewrote a surface most people use for things that are not AI at all. Its title cue
"Bing" went with it. SitePolicyStore.ProxyExcludedHosts still names bing.com and is now inert rather than
wrong - left in place because the reason it was excluded (never MITM a general-purpose product) is the rule,
not the host, and the next such host must inherit it.
REMOVED FROM THE REDACTED TIER on 30 August 2026 (HUMAN-ACTIONS W8.14, AI-TODO A22):
azure.microsoft.com, designer.microsoft.com and deepmind.google. All three were documentation or
marketing surfaces with no chat composer, so the injected script stood down on every one of them: they
cost an access permission and bought nothing, while `verified` claimed coverage nothing had exercised.
designer.microsoft.com went too even though it is an image tool where uploads happen with nothing to
type into - a partial exception would have re-created exactly the claim the removal exists to retire.
The three are NOT added to the blocked tier. Blocking would close a Microsoft documentation site and a
research page some users legitimately want open, a cost the decision did not ask for. They are simply
unlisted now, which is what every other site on the internet is.
Microsoft AI KEEPS `Microsoft Designer` in `titles`, deliberately. `titles` is the window-title fallback
for NATIVE apps (SitePolicyStore.ProtectedNativeApp) - a different channel from hosts, and W8.14 decided
the host tier. Removing it would have changed native-app behaviour nothing decided.
TWO of the five remain unexercised and inherit the company flag without evidence of their own:
platform.openai.com and copilot.cloud.microsoft. Both have real composers, so they need a live pass
rather than a decision - AI-TODO A17.
notebook.google.com ADDED 31 August 2026, AND A VENDOR RENAME HAD LEFT IT COMPLETELY UNPROTECTED FOR SIX
WEEKS. Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook on 16 July 2026 and moved it to notebook.google.com.
That host was in NO tier - not redacted, not blocked - so the content script was never injected and typing
there was watched by nothing. Reported by a user typing two names into it and seeing neither redacted.
notebooklm.google.com is KEPT alongside it: an old bookmark or a redirect must not lose protection, and
removing a host is the one edit here that can only ever remove cover.
It is ALSO unexercised and inherits `verified` from the company, so it belongs on A17's list with the two
above. That is the safe direction and it is not a free pass: protection running on an unexercised host is
better than no protection, and the claim is tracked rather than assumed.
THE RENAME WAS HALF-SEEN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING. The blocked-tier Google Gemini entry had
already gained `Gemini Notebook` in its `titles` - so somebody noticed the new NAME and updated the
native-app matcher, while the new HOST was never added anywhere. Titles and hosts are different channels
and a rename touches both; updating one reads as having handled it. See AI-TODO A32.
Recording it here rather than silently, because the rule this project already fixed once was exactly this:
decorating a site we cannot protect is worse than leaving it alone, since a highlight reads as a promise.
TWO TIERS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS NOT OPTIONAL. The four entries below are REDACTED: verified, redact:true,
and the only ones the browser extension is ever told to watch. Everything after them is BLOCKED: redact is
false and verified is absent, so BuildHostCompanyMap excludes them and no content script is injected, but
blocked:true puts their hosts into BlockedHosts() and from there into a declarativeNetRequest rule and the
proxy PAC blackhole tier, so the site does not open at all.
The blocked tier was briefly DELETED when the list was consolidated onto four vendors, and that was a
fail-open regression rather than a simplification: removing an entry does not just stop us redacting a
service, it stops us RECOGNISING it, so ~345 AI sites the product had always refused to open began loading
normally with no protection of any kind. Blocking what we cannot redact is the fail-closed answer.
NO BLOCKED HOST MAY EQUAL, CONTAIN OR SIT UNDER A REDACTED ONE. Block rules match a domain AND its
subdomains, so a blocked parent would blackhole a redacted child - blocking anthropic.com would have closed
console.anthropic.com. Eight hosts were dropped for that reason when this tier was rebuilt:
gemini.google.com, aistudio.google.com, notebooklm.google.com, copilot.microsoft.com,
huggingface.co and labs.google moved to blocked tier on 18 Oct 2026. edgeservices.bing.com went when bing.com itself was
removed on 7 September 2026, and Microsoft Bing had already lost its only host that way. A test asserts
tiers never intersect in any of those three directions.
PROMPT APPLICATIONS ONLY. Microsoft AI's apps.processes lists Copilot and nothing else. It used to list
WINWORD, EXCEL, POWERPNT and OUTLOOK too, because those host a Copilot pane and pasting into that pane was
therefore covered. The cost was not worth it: an email client is not a prompt application, and treating it
as one put a redaction preview over an email the user had merely RECEIVED (1.10.0). Word, Excel,
PowerPoint and Outlook are now out of the redacting set entirely - no paste protection, no overlay, no
send gate - on the owner's instruction that only AI prompt applications are redacted.
THE FOUR STAY IN send_gate_exempt_processes, and that list now means NEVER AN AI DESTINATION rather than
merely 'do not hold Enter here'. Removing them from apps.processes alone was not enough: a native app that
matches no process still falls back to WINDOW TITLE matching, and this company's titles include the whole
word 'Copilot' - so an email whose subject mentioned Copilot would have been read as an AI destination and
the overlay would have returned on exactly the surface this change exists to clear. The JSON key keeps its
name for schema stability; the C# accessor is SitePolicyStore.NeverAnAiDestination, which says what it does.
GOOGLE AI GAINED AN apps BLOCK ON 16 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND THE STATE IT REPLACED WAS THE WORST AVAILABLE.
Google shipped a native Gemini client for Windows in September 2026 (gemini.google/desktop, summoned with
Alt+Space). This entry had been hosts-and-titles only, and the two resolvers disagree about what that means:
NativeSendGuard, LiveTypingWatcher and NativeUnredactionWatcher go through ProtectedNativeApp, which falls
back to WINDOW TITLE, so 'Gemini' matched and the Enter/click send gate engaged - and then refused every send,
because VerifiedOnlyRefusal asks IsVerifiedApp and this company carried no verified_app. Meanwhile
PasteHookService, DragDropWarnService, NativeFilePickerGuard and the delayed-clipboard predicate all go
through ProtectedByApp, which needs an apps block and had none - so pasting into that same window handed over
the raw original. The product was blocking the app from sending AND leaking what was pasted into it.
MEASURED AGAINST REAL INSTALLS ON 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 (spike S-App). Every apps value below is now either read
from a running client or explicitly marked unverified. Evidence: analytics/native-ai-app-probe.md, regenerate
with tools/probe-native-ai-apps.ps1. THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THREE OF THE FOUR ENTRIES, and two of the three
were matching NOTHING - the seeded values were not merely imprecise, they were inert:
GOOGLE AI. Measured: process 'Gemini' (the UI process; there are also GeminiAppLauncher and
GeminiCrashpadHandler, all three reporting ProductName 'Gemini', CompanyName 'Google LLC'), window class
Chrome_WidgetWin_0 - an Electron client - and NOT PACKAGED. So 'GoogleGemini' and 'GeminiDesktop' were
invented spellings matching nothing and are gone, the Google.Gemini package guess is gone because the client
is a Win32 install and no Store package exists to guess at, and GeminiAppLauncher is now named because the
Alt+Space summon surface is the launcher's, not the renderer's. 'Gemini' was right all along, so this entry
was working; the other two were not.
MICROSOFT AI. Measured: process 'M365Copilot', ProductName 'Microsoft 365 Copilot'. THE PREVIOUS VALUES
MATCHED NEITHER. Process matching is exact, so 'Copilot' does not match 'M365Copilot'; product matching is a
substring test, and 'Microsoft Copilot' is not a substring of 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' - the '365' sits
between the two words. So the shipped Microsoft Copilot desktop app was recognised by no identity signal at
all: the same hole Google AI was in, in the same product, undetected because nothing was asking. Both
measured strings are now listed, and the old ones kept, because a standalone Copilot.exe exists on some
Windows builds and an exact spelling costs nothing.
Its package family is Microsoft.MicrosoftOfficeHub_8wekyb3d8bbwe and is DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED. M365Copilot
ships inside the Office Hub package, which also hosts the plain 'Office' app - so naming that family would
make Office itself an AI destination, which is the opposite of the prompt-applications-only rule above. The
process signal is exact and sufficient; a package signal here would be broader than the thing it identifies.
ANTHROPIC. Measured: an MSIX install whose package family is 'Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc'. 'AnthropicPBC.Claude'
matched nothing - the resolver accepts the bare family NAME or the name plus its publisher suffix, and the
publisher id is not part of the name. The entry is now 'Claude', which the prefix rule expands to
'Claude_<publisherId>' and so survives a republish under a new publisher id. Its process name could not be
re-read because the app was not running at measurement time; 'claude' is unchanged and unverified.
OPENAI IS UNVERIFIED. The ChatGPT desktop client is not installed on the measuring machine, so its process,
product and package values are still the originally seeded ones. Recorded rather than quietly presented as
measured, because 'we checked' and 'we assumed' have to stay distinguishable - that distinction is the whole
reason the Microsoft entry above went unnoticed.
WHAT THE MEASUREMENT DID NOT ANSWER: whether either client's composer exposes a UI Automation ValuePattern
or TextPattern, which is what the typing overlay and the Enter/send rewrite need. Both apps were running
with their windows hidden, and Chromium builds its accessibility tree only on demand, so the walk returned a
bare root - see analytics/native-composer-probe.md and tools/probe-native-composer.ps1, which has to be run
with the window OPEN. Paste, drag and the file picker do not need a pattern and are unaffected either way.
DEEPSEEK CARRIES web_only BECAUSE THERE IS NO FIRST-PARTY WINDOWS CLIENT. Users install the website as a PWA
through Edge or Chrome, which runs inside the browser process and is therefore the extension's territory, or
they use one of several unofficial Electron/Tauri/WebView2 wrappers. Those wrappers are NOT enumerated here
and must not be: a curated list of third-party builds is wrong most of the time and its failure mode is a
leak, which is the same argument AI-TODO.md A13.7 makes about growing ProxyInterceptHosts. They are covered
by the window-title tier (send gate, live typing, restore) and by the PAC observe tier. The flag exists so
'this company has no apps block' can be a DELIBERATE answer rather than an oversight - the state Google AI
was in above - and so the test that requires every redacting company to declare one has something to read.
AN apps BLOCK ON A **BLOCKED** COMPANY NOW MEANS SOMETHING, AND IT MEANS THE OPPOSITE OF THE ONES ABOVE.
Perplexity is the first: it is blocked, it does not redact, and it ships an official Windows installer. That
combination used to be the only surface in the product with NO answer at all - its websites were blackholed
while the same service's desktop program worked perfectly, so the block was one download away from being
irrelevant. It could not be redacted (this entry says do not) and it was not refused, because the only
resolver that looked at apps was ProtectedByApp, which requires the redact flag.
SitePolicyStore.RefusedNativeApp now reads apps on EVERY tier and answers 'refuse this program's send
gesture', which is the native equivalent of blackholing a website - ARCHITECTURE.md's rule that for native
apps the send gesture is refused rather than the process. Two things follow for whoever edits this file:
* ONLY ADD apps HERE FOR A NAMED, OFFICIAL DESKTOP CLIENT OF A REAL AI SERVICE. The refusal fails CLOSED,
so a wrong entry stops somebody working in a program that was never an AI client. There is deliberately
no title matching and no name heuristic on this path.
* NEVER ADD apps TO A LOCAL MODEL RUNNER (Ollama, LM Studio, GPT4All, Jan, Msty, AnythingLLM). Nothing
typed into those leaves the machine, so refusing their send removes the safest option the user has. The
code exempts local: true for exactly this reason, but those entries no longer carry the flag, so the
guard here is editorial: do not add the block.
* DO NOT ADD apps TO A GENERAL-PURPOSE PRODUCT with an AI side-feature (Canva, Notion, Asana, Airtable and
the rest). Blocking a design tool or a note-taker because it grew an assistant is the exact harm that
retired VerifiedOnlyMode and that the monday.com/notion.so report was about. A dedicated AI client is
the whole test for belonging here.
The process and product values are seeded from the published installer name ('Perplexity Setup x.y.z-x64.exe')
and are narrowed by measurement like every other apps block - see NATIVE-APP-DROP-AND-ATTACH-PLAN.md, S-App.

data.web_only_why: No first-party Windows client exists. Users install the website as a PWA, which runs inside the browser process and is therefore the extension's territory, or they use an unofficial Electron/Tauri/WebView2 wrapper - and those are deliberately not enumerated (see the _data_note). Remove this flag the day DeepSeek ships an official desktop app, and add an apps block read from a real install.
